card.notes:
FAILURES, stated plainly.
(1) C3 fails at ε=1/2. r3 (0.02178) sits above r1 (0.02132), so the observed order is r2 > r3 > r1, not the predicted r2 > r1 > r3. The gap (−0.00046) is far inside the seed spreads (r1 sd 0.00298, r3 sd 0.00133). Unscored context: the evaluation raws' exact KIND KL at k=7 (kind_kl_bits) gives r1 0.02191 > r3 0.02159, the predicted direction, by 0.0003. So this link can't be resolved at 3 seeds and flips with the estimator. The stamped estimator is census by_field.kind, and under it C3 fails. The evaluation raws' structural_by_field.kind equals the census means exactly (difference 0 in all 27 runs), which independently confirms the C3/C4 inputs.
(2) Relay primary R1 fails only on the band. The slope is positive and strongly significant (t 6.24), but 0.016273 is just under the 0.0165 floor, about 0.09 se below it. Under the literal stamped wording ("its value lies in [0.0165, 0.066]") that is a FAIL. No stamped reading uses a CI.
(3) R2 fails by a lot. The exact-zero set's mean Δexcess (+0.00076) is about 0 but well below the intercept (+0.00458, t 10.2). The intercept is the prereg's "generic effect of the new field", and it doesn't hold on the exact-zero set. R2 fails under either se reading.
(4) R4 fails in the opposite direction: on Δι < −0.05 windows the r1R models are significantly better (quadrature t +3.42, set-se t +3.51). The secondary arm goes the same way (t +2.55 / +2.62).
Surprise, unscored, for the owner: addendum §4 says the deciles of Δι are reported, but relay_paired.py doesn't compute them. I computed them in scratch by importing the frozen functions unchanged (~/.cache/yupi-scratch/census/relay-deciles/relay-deciles-2026-10-02.json). In the primary arm Δexcess is V-shaped in Δι: dec0 (mean Δι −0.157) +0.0109, dec1 +0.0033, dec2 +0.0019, dec3 (around 0) +0.0007, dec4 +0.0039 … dec8 +0.0102, dec9 (mean Δι +0.620) +0.0153. So r1R's advantage grows with |Δι| in both directions, not with signed Δι. That is why R4 has the wrong sign and R2's set sits below the intercept. I haven't investigated a confound; one candidate is that |Δι| tracks window difficulty. In the secondary arm the slope disappears (t 0.21), but the V shape on the negative side is still there.
AMBIGUITIES. (a) C3 is one prediction with two parts. I scored each part and the whole (FAIL because the ε=1/2 chain breaks). The ε=1/2 r2>r3 pair is implied by the chain, not separately stamped, so I list it as REPORTED. (b) A4 uses the row the actor verdict scored (full_plus_log2_class_mass); the 'full' no-mass model also gives 24/24. The two narrowest margins on the scored row are t 3.07 and 3.17. (c) R4: addendum §2 governs, so the scored t is the quadrature t (t_with_intercept_se), even though relay_paired.py's own in-file verdict uses the set-se t. Both readings FAIL here, so the choice changes nothing. (d) The C3/C4 cross-check against 'the raw's class list' can only be partial: each census raw lists only the top 20 classes (window share 0.2–8%) out of about 28k. For those classes, n matches and by_field.kind matches the per-window rows to within 2e-16. Row count equals summary.n and the structural mean equals summary.mean exactly, in all 30 runs.
OTHER OBSERVATIONS. C2 passes, but converged pooled β_long (0.013–0.025) is about 40% below the 5-epoch values (0.029–0.041). At ε=1, the pooled KIND β_short now has t 2.4–4.4 in r2, r3 and r4. R3 primary passes, with r1R's own pooled β_long 0.0179. Provenance: r1 ε=1 e15 seed2 (a pre-existing model) resumed from step 38000 and finished at 117195. The new census raws record git 680dafe+dirty because learner_window_census.py checks the whole tree (`git status --porcelain` with no path filter) while sibling raws were being written to docs/; that's harmless. The frozen KIND bintest writes a hardcoded status 'EXPLORATORY (paper-1 readiness item 3, all windows)' into its raws, including these confirmatory ones; that's cosmetic. Nothing committed; the GPU wasn't touched; no processes killed. Untracked new files: the 7 docs/*.json raws listed and scripts/converged_ladder_c3c4.py.

objections.claim: The scorecard checks only C2's band. The stamped C2 text goes on to say: 'The prediction is that convergence shrinks the long-lag cost no more than the overall excess shrinks, and does not remove it.' The scorecard never evaluates that sentence. Read literally, as part of the prediction, it fails in 8/8 cells: β_long fell proportionally more than the excess in every cell. The wording is ambiguous, so both readings are given. Reading A (the band is the operational criterion, the sentence is its rationale; commit 05e3543's message summarises C2 as just 'pooled β_long in [0.01,0.05]'): C2 PASS 8/8. Reading B (the sentence labelled 'The prediction is' is scored too): C2 FAIL 8/8. The 'does not remove it' clause passes under both readings.
objections.evidence: My recomputation compares pooled β_long on full_plus_log2_class_mass at 5 epochs (docs/implicit-info-bintest-freqctl-k7-2026-09-29.json for ε=1, docs/d1-long-lag-heldout-primary-2026-09-29.json for ε=½) with 15 epochs (docs/converged-ladder-bintest-kind-2026-10-02.json). It sets that against the pooled mean KIND excess (mean_excess in the same raws). Ratios are 15-epoch over 5-epoch, β vs KIND excess. r1 ε=1: 0.477 vs 0.720. r1 ε=½: 0.542 vs 0.632. r2 ε=1 (seeds 1–3): 0.580 vs 0.662; with seeds 4–6 as the 5-epoch reference, 0.766 vs 0.829. r2 ε=½: 0.599 vs 0.777. r3 ε=1: 0.548 vs 0.700. r3 ε=½: 0.689 vs 0.737. r4 ε=1: 0.452 vs 0.575. r4 ε=½: 0.552 vs 0.670. The total structural excess (census summary.mean) gives the same direction everywhere. Its ratios are 0.56–0.79, e.g. r1 ε=1 0.774 and r4 ε=½ 0.702 (6 seeds) or 0.568 (seeds 1–3), each still above the matching β ratio. These are point-estimate comparisons. r3 ε=½ (0.689 vs 0.737) is likely within noise, but the literal wording has no uncertainty allowance. Some cells mix 6-seed 5-epoch pools with 3-seed 15-epoch pools. That changes no direction.

objections.claim: The C3/C4 computation script was written after the raws existed, and it was never frozen or stamped. The runner discloses this. The script does compute what was stamped: the plain mean of by_field.kind over every row of the k=7 test per-window file (rows = windows with ≥7 records, n = summary.n), with gates on k=7, the test split, a full census, and step 117195. The cell mean is the mean of the three seed means; per-seed n is equal, so this equals the pooled window mean. Seed resolution is min(hi) > max(lo). My code is independent of that script and reproduces every C3/C4 number exactly. The verdict should still say the scoring script for C3/C4 is post-hoc code for a stamped estimator. Minor wording: the scorecard says eval structural_by_field.kind equals the census means with 'difference 0'; the measured maximum is 4.7e-16.
objections.evidence: My independent read of all 36 per-window files: sha256 matches in 36/36, and the cell means match the scorecard to 5 decimals. ε=½: r1 0.02132, r2 0.02929, r3 0.02178, r4 0.02304, r0 0.00489. ε=1: r1 0.01536, r2 0.01887, r3 0.01344, r4 0.01329, r0 0.00383. OBJECTION DISPOSITIONS
1. C2 shrink clause (claude, changes-result): ACCEPTED. The stamped C2 text includes "The prediction is that convergence shrinks the long-lag cost no more than the overall excess shrinks, and does not remove it." Round 1 never evaluated it. I checked it two ways.
   - Matched seeds: I re-ran the frozen bintest on the 5-epoch seed 1-3 censuses, into scratch. The reviewer's mix of 6-seed and 3-seed pools doesn't decide the result.
   - Two readings of "overall excess": the KIND excess (by_field.kind mean) and the total structural excess (census summary.mean).
   In all 8 cells, β_long shrank proportionally more than either excess, so the shrink clause fails 8/8. "Does not remove it" passes 8/8.
   - Reading A (the band is the criterion; commit 05e3543's message summarises C2 as the band alone): PASS 8/8.
   - Reading B (the sentence headed "The prediction is" is scored too): FAIL 8/8.
   I scored C2 AMBIGUOUS overall and give both readings. My own view: the literal text favours Reading B. The sentence is introduced as the prediction, and the band [0.01,0.05] cannot test it, since the band would accept a three- to four-fold β drop no matter how much the excess fell.
   Caveats (unscored): the comparison has to be proportional (ratio), because β is bits per bit and excess is bits. The narrowest cell is r3 ε=½, with β ratio 0.689 against KIND 0.737, a gap of about 0.8 of a rough delta-method se. That se uses pooled, not seed-clustered, se and ignores the correlation between budgets on the same windows. The wording has no noise allowance. Five cells separate by 2 to 4.7 such se.
2. C3 r2>r3 at ε=½ label (claude): ACCEPTED. "ranks as ι_kind,4 ranks (r2 > r1 > r3)" is a full three-cell ranking, so r2>r3 is a stamped component. It is now scored PASS on means and not seed-resolved. The script's mean_order_holds uses pairs[:2], which is equivalent to all three pairs by transitivity, so no recomputation was needed and the script was not changed. C3 is still FAIL.
3. and 7. Relay-field excess (claude, codex): ACCEPTED. Added REPORTED lines for both arms from relay_field_excess_r1R: primary 9.38e-5 (se 1.79e-6), secondary 1.73e-4 (se 3.31e-5).
4. and 8. Deciles (claude, codex): ACCEPTED. Added REPORTED lines with all ten bins for each arm. I also corrected round 1's description of the secondary arm: it rises on the negative side, but at the top dec9 (+0.0033) falls back below dec7 and dec8, so it is not monotone or V-shaped on the positive side. The lines state that the numbers come from post-hoc scratch code. That code imports the frozen relay_paired functions unchanged, and both reviewers reproduced it independently.
5. Cache sha provenance (claude): ACCEPTED. I verified it myself: actorgk 10/10, r1R ι cache 91d4f0a2…, Δι table 0501876c…. All are recorded in sha_checks now. No results changed.
6. C3/C4 post-hoc script disclosure, and 'difference 0' (claude): ACCEPTED. The C3 overall line now says the scorer is post-hoc, unstamped code implementing the stamped estimator, and that an independent reviewer reproduced it exactly. I re-measured max |eval − per-window mean| at 4.7e-16, not 0. Round 1 had compared eval against the census raw's recorded aggregate. The checkpoint sha matches 27/27.
9. r1 ε=1 between-seed spread (codex): ACCEPTED. C4/eps1-with-r1 now lists r1's seeds (0.01570 0.01464 0.01576, sd 0.00063). The other cells' sds are now given in the C4 lines too.

- C2 fails under Reading B.
